newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin sends chemical arms pact to parliament.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin sends chemical arms pact to parliament.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin on Monday sent the international treaty on chemical weapons to parliament for ratification, his office said, just days before he is scheduled to meet U.S. President Bill Clinton in Helsinki.

The 1993 treaty goes into force on April 29, and has not been ratified by either the United States or Russia, which hold the world's largest chemical weapons arsenals. The Clinton administration has stepped up efforts to win U.S. Senate approval.
Yeltsin in 1993 signed the treaty, which bars states from acquiring, stockpiling, transferring or using chemical weapons. More than 160 countries have signed the pact.

"For Russia the main obstacle has been the lack of financing," Yeltsin's office said in a statement. "At present, the executive and legislative branch are seeking ways to procure funds to fulfil the complete program of chemical disarmament.
